chunks: The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:
I said to Abu Ja'far عليه السلام: May a man perform, with one tayammum, the prayer of the night and the whole day? He said: Yes, so long as he does not invalidate it or find water.

key_terms.اللَّيْلِ: the night, referring here to night prayers
key_terms.النَّهَارِ: the day, referring here to daytime prayers
key_terms.الْمَاءَ: water, whose availability ends the concession of tayammum
key_terms.بِتَيَمُّمٍ: with tayammum, the dry ablution used in place of wudu (ablution) or ghusl (ritual bath)
key_terms.يُحْدِثْ: to enter a state of ritual invalidation

ai.seo_question: Can a person pray multiple prayers with one tayammum?
ai.summary: This hadith states that one tayammum is sufficient for multiple prayers, including the prayers of the night and day. Its validity continues unless the person enters a state requiring renewal or finds water.
